author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it named first name then last name, all on one page.
acceptance_criteria: Opening /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name.
Under each specialty, every veterinarian holding it is named as first name followed by last name, such as "Helen Leary".
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is named under each specialty held.
A veterinarian holding no specialty is named nowhere on the page.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it.
Every specialty renders on the one page; no paging control is offered and no page parameter changes what is shown.
A clinic that knows no specialties opens an empty directory rather than failing.
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order across repeated requests.
No other page carries a link or a navigation entry leading to the specialty directory.
The specialty directory carries the same navigation every page carries under REQ-SYS-001.
The page's own wording resolves from the message bundles in every supported language; specialty names render as stored, untranslated.
non_goals: Creating, renaming, or deleting specialties, and assigning them to veterinarians - NG-2 is unchanged and this view is read-only.
A navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory; the address is the only way in. Named as a possible follow-up request, not declined.
A machine-readable variant of the specialty list - REQ-VET-002 was withdrawn and nothing revives that shape.
Paging, sorting controls, filtering, or search over the specialty directory.
Changing REQ-VET-001: the veterinarian list keeps its paging and its vet-to-specialty direction.
notes: Boundary check: no contradiction with REQ-VET-001 (different page, inverse index, unpaged), REQ-SYS-001 (it governs what a page carries, not what points at it), or NG-2 (read-only). Open questions taken at the narrowest reading and recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions: (1) presentation order is unspecified - the requirement asks only for a stable order, not a named one; (2) a visible entry point is deferred, not declined. Two further readings taken narrowly and stated in the requirement rather than left open: a specialty held by nobody is still listed, since the page lists every specialty the clinic knows; and specialty names render as stored while the page chrome is localized, which is what "by its stored name" plus REQ-LANG-002 jointly require. Slice is single-surface (code, with its tests) and sized for one inner-loop cycle.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The page is a conventional feature-package slice: a third @GetMapping on VetController, a Thymeleaf view under templates/vets, and a Spring Data repository, all inside the vet package (docs/system-design.md Package Structure, ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). One element is genuinely new ground: the veterinarian-specialty association is mapped only from Vet to Specialty, so the specialty-to-vet direction this page needs exists nowhere. It is derived in memory by a new SpecialtyDirectory value object rather than by an inverse @ManyToMany or an inverting query - recorded in ADR 2026-08-22-in-memory-specialty-to-veterinarian-inversion, with the association-direction rule and the vets cache-key fact added to docs/system-design.md Contracts. SpecialtyDirectory is the first realization of the pattern catalog's Value object row, and it is what keeps the grouping out of the controller, which the catalog's Web controller row forbids.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html -> new handler on VetController; view name vets/specialtyList; one model attribute, specialtyDirectory. No page parameter is bound and no pagination helper is reused.

SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> (the marker interface VetRepository uses, not JpaRepository - the narrow surface is what keeps NG-2's read-only stance structural). One method: @Transactional(readOnly = true) List<Specialty> findSpecialties(); with @Query("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name"), mirroring PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes(). No @Cacheable.
VetController gains SpecialtyRepository as a second constructor argument; the existing VetRepository dependency and both existing routes are unchanged.
Veterinarians come from the existing cached VetRepository.findAll() - unpaged and with specialties already loaded by the EAGER @ManyToMany.

SpecialtyDirectory.of(List<Specialty>, Collection<Vet>) performs the inversion: specialties in the order given, each paired with the veterinarians whose specialties contain it. The controller binds, delegates to this factory, and selects the view - it holds no rule.

Template extends the shared layout as ~{fragments/layout :: layout (~{::body},'specialties')}; the menu key matches no menuItem, so REQ-SYS-001 navigation renders with nothing highlighted and no link to the page is added anywhere.

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository with an explicit ORDER BY query - the form SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() copies
narrow Repository<T, ID> marker surface exposing only the read methods the app needs - the base interface SpecialtyRepository copies
layout fragment call, table markup, and the ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName} full-name expression the new template reuses
Value object row - SpecialtyDirectory and its entries are immutable, equal by value, built by a static factory, with defensive copies of both lists

risks.risk: @Cacheable("vets") copied onto findSpecialties(). The vets cache is keyed by arguments alone, so a second no-argument method collides with VetRepository.findAll() and returns Collection<Vet> where List<Specialty> is expected - a ClassCastException at runtime that no compile step catches.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository carries no caching annotation at all. Caching this query later needs its own cache name declared in CacheConfiguration; this slice adds none.

risks.risk: Reaching for an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) on Specialty, or an @EntityGraph / fetch join on VetRepository.findAll(), to get the inverse direction or to kill the per-vet specialty select.
risks.mitigation: Both are out of scope and both are rejected in ADR 2026-08-22. findAll() is shared with /vets.html and /vets; the Vet and Specialty mappings stay exactly as they are. The per-vet select is the pre-existing N+1 on the eager @ManyToMany, bounded by the clinic's roster size and served from the vets cache - this slice neither worsens nor fixes it.

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory declared package-private for minimal surface. Thymeleaf reads model attributes through SpEL reflection, which fails on accessors declared in a non-public class - which is why Vet, Specialty, and Vets are all public.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory and its entry type are public. VetController and SpecialtyRepository keep their existing visibility.

risks.risk: I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build on the new template. It flags any literal >text< in an HTML file under src/main that carries no #{...} or th:text, and it flags any key present in messages.properties but missing from a locale bundle.
risks.mitigation: Every fixed string in specialtyList.html resolves through #{...}; every new key is added to messages.properties and to all locale bundles except messages_en (which the test skips by design). Specialty names and veterinarian names come from the model through th:text and stay untranslated, which is what REQ-LANG-002 requires.

risks.risk: Ordering left to the persistence layer or to HashSet iteration, making the page unstable across requests.
risks.mitigation: Specialties are ordered by the repository's ORDER BY name. Veterinarians under each specialty are ordered inside SpecialtyDirectory.of by last name then first name - VetRepository.findAll() returns an unordered Collection and Vet.specialties is a HashSet, so neither can be relied on.

notes: Verdict is new rather than minor because the slice introduces the codebase's first value object, a repository for a type that had none, and a durable rule about the association direction - all three needed recording. Two deviations from the prd-entry's file_targets, both deliberate: the specialty query goes on a new SpecialtyRepository rather than on VetRepository (Repository is one per aggregate root, and VetRepository is typed to Vet), and SpecialtyDirectory is a new file the prd-entry did not anticipate. The route stays on VetController rather than a new SpecialtyController: one read-only GET with no binding or validation does not earn a type, and the owner package's controller split is driven by form workflows this page has none of. Acceptance criteria, non-goals, and test names are the prd-entry's verbatim; SpecialtyDirectoryTests is named here as the natural home for the inversion tests, but where the seven named tests land is the testing-strategist's call. Note for that call: the inversion is a pure function over real Vet and Specialty instances and needs no Spring context, so testing-principles' no-mocks default applies to it directly, whatever VetControllerTests does with @MockitoBean today. Edge cases map as follows: a specialty nobody holds is an entry with an empty veterinarian list, and empty inputs give an empty directory that the template renders as an empty page - neither is a branch in the controller. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. No trust boundary is introduced: the route takes no parameter, reads no user input, and Thymeleaf's default escaping covers the rendered names, as it does on /vets.html.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: JPQL in SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a compile-time constant with no parameters, no bind variables and no string concatenation; no injection surface is introduced. Verified no other concatenated query strings exist in the diff.

Output escaping verified rather than assumed: templates/vets/specialtyList.html uses th:text exclusively (specialty name at line 18, veterinarian names at line 21) and th:utext appears nowhere in the file. A repository-wide sweep of src/main/resources/templates confirms no th:utext, no th:inline, and no expression preprocessing (__${...}__) in the new template, so Thymeleaf HTML-mode default escaping applies to every model-derived value the page renders. The SpEL concatenation at line 21 is evaluated before escaping, so its result is escaped as one string. This matches the system-design threat-model row for cross-site scripting.

GET /specialties.html binds no request parameter, path variable, header or body; the handler takes only Model. The design triage claim that the slice introduces no new trust boundary holds against the code: no untrusted value enters the new code path, so no new validation or binder restriction is owed.

No new information disclosure class. Specialty names and veterinarian names are already served unauthenticated by the pre-existing /vets.html page and the /vets JSON endpoint; the new page re-presents the same roster fields with no additional attributes (no identifiers, contact details or PII beyond the already-published names). The application-wide absence of authentication is a pre-existing condition recorded in docs/system-design.md, not something this slice changes.

Defensive copying is correct on both records: SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyDirectory.Entry each run List.copyOf in their compact constructor, so the exposed lists are immutable and no caller can mutate directory state after construction.

SpecialtyDirectory.of does not mutate the entities it reads. holdersBySpecialtyId builds fresh HashMap/ArrayList structures and holdersOf returns a newly sorted list, so the @Cacheable 'vets' collection shared into this path is not written through - no cache-poisoning surface.

Load surface assessed and cleared as non-blocking: the unpaged listing plus the uncached specialty query add work per request, but the request is unauthenticated-read-only over data already served unpaged by the existing /vets endpoint, and the bound is the clinic's specialty and veterinarian row count, not attacker-controlled input. No amplification factor exists. Recorded as an operational note for the design owner, not a security finding.

Supply chain clean: the change set touches no build.gradle, pom.xml, properties, or manifest file, so no dependency is added, removed or version-shifted and no new CVE surface enters through this slice. No hardcoded credential, token, key or other secret appears anywhere in the diff.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The nested record is named `Entry`, the exact placeholder name `docs/architecture-principles.md` § Naming calls out by name as prohibited: "Names come from the project's canonical vocabulary... if the PRD calls it a 'feed item', the code says FeedItem, never Entry or Record." `ubiquitous-language.md` already supplies the vocabulary this pairing needs — a Specialty is 'held by' zero or more Veterinarians, and the ADR/system-design prose both say 'the veterinarians holding it'. A name built on that verb (e.g. `SpecialtyDirectory.Holding`) reads as the domain concept it is instead of a generic container placeholder.
findings.fix: Rename `SpecialtyDirectory.Entry` to a domain-derived name (e.g. `Holding`, pairing a Specialty with the veterinarians holding it) and update its two use sites in `SpecialtyDirectory.java` (the `entries` field type/construction) and the one reference in `SpecialtyDirectoryTests.java:63`. The Thymeleaf template accesses fields by record-component name (`entry.specialty`, `entry.veterinarians`), not by the type name, so `specialtyList.html` needs no change beyond the local loop-variable name if desired.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyRepository correctly omits @Cacheable and documents why, avoiding the vets-cache collision the design forbids
Specialty/VetRepository mappings left untouched — no inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) and no @EntityGraph/fetch join added to findAll()
SpecialtyDirectory and its nested record are public with a javadoc explaining the Thymeleaf SpEL-reflection reason
Holder matching keyed on Specialty.getId() with a javadoc explaining why, consistent with the no-equals/hashCode constraint
Explicit ordering at both levels: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() carries an ORDER BY, and SpecialtyDirectory.of sorts veterinarians by last-then-first name
Records use compact constructors with List.copyOf for defensive immutability
VetController wiring follows the existing constructor-injection and show-prefixed-method conventions in the file

Template and message-key reuse (specialties/name/vets) mirrors the existing vetList.html pattern exactly, and the unmatched 'specialties' menu argument yields standard layout navigation with no nav highlight, matching the URL-only reachability requirement
checkFormat passes with no formatting issues

author: test-reviewer

VetControllerTests stubs findSpecialties() with Mockito, so the JPQL text itself is never parsed or run. ClinicServiceTests is the established @DataJpaTest integration test for this exact repository shape (it already autowires the sibling PetTypeRepository and asserts findPetTypes() against the real H2-backed schema, per docs/system-design.md's cited pattern at PetTypeRepository.java:36) but was not extended for SpecialtyRepository. The brief's Mocking Policy requires real I/O for integration coverage, and this is the one query in the slice that has none.
findings.fix: Add `@Autowired protected SpecialtyRepository specialties;` to ClinicServiceTests and a test (e.g. theSpecialtyRepositoryShouldReturnSpecialtiesOrderedByName) that calls specialties.findSpecialties() against the real test database and asserts the returned list is ordered by name, mirroring the existing PetType assertions in that file.

approved_aspects: All 7 required test_names from the prd-entry are present and pass: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNameEachVeterinarianFirstNameThenLastName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListAVeterinarianUnderEverySpecialtyHeld, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitAVeterinarianHoldingNoSpecialty, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyNoVeterinarianHolds, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderEverySpecialtyOnOnePage, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderEmptyWhenNoSpecialtyExists

SpecialtyDirectoryTests is a pure unit suite with no Spring context, real value objects throughout, BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming, four-phase structure, and named/anonymous test data (RADIOLOGY_ID, SOME_SPECIALTY_NAME) with no mystery literals

Cross-load identity-matching risk from the design-block is directly pinned by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldMatchASpecialtyLoadedAsASeparateInstance, using two distinct Specialty instances sharing an id exactly as the ADR describes
Stable-ordering contract covered on both axes: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldKeepTheGivenSpecialtyOrder and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansByLastNameThenFirstName
Defensive-copy immutability covered by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNotChangeWhenTheGivenCollectionsChange

VetControllerTests's use of @MockitoBean on VetRepository/SpecialtyRepository is the project's pre-existing, brief-tolerated web-slice pattern (boundary mock at the persistence layer under a real MockMvc dispatch), not new mocking territory
No-pagination behavior verified with realistic data sized past the vet list's page size (8 specialties vs. the 5-per-page vet list), matching the design-block's stated risk mitigation
All 16 tests (8 unit + 8 web-slice) pass under ./gradlew test; jacoco reports 100% line/branch coverage on the vet package, above the brief's 80% target

risks.risk: The recorded route drifts from the @GetMapping on VetController, leaving durable memory naming an address the application no longer serves.
risks.mitigation: The address is stated once, in the Contracts section, next to the VetController row that points at the source file; the source stays authoritative for everything else about the handler. A route change is a change to external contract and re-enters through the pipeline, where this paragraph is the single place to update.

risks.risk: @Cacheable("vets") copied onto findSpecialties(). The vets cache is keyed by arguments alone, so a second no-argument method collides with VetRepository.findAll() and returns Collection<Vet> where List<Specialty> is expected - a ClassCastException at runtime that no compile step catches.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository carries no caching annotation at all. Caching this query later needs its own cache name declared in CacheConfiguration; this slice adds none.

risks.risk: Reaching for an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) on Specialty, or an @EntityGraph / fetch join on VetRepository.findAll(), to get the inverse direction or to kill the per-vet specialty select.
risks.mitigation: Both are out of scope and both are rejected in ADR 2026-08-22. findAll() is shared with /vets.html and /vets; the Vet and Specialty mappings stay exactly as they are. The per-vet select is the pre-existing N+1 on the eager @ManyToMany, bounded by the clinic's roster size and served from the vets cache - this slice neither worsens nor fixes it.

risks.risk: Pairing the two sides on Specialty object identity or equals. No persisted type in this codebase overrides equals or hashCode, and the vets arrive from the cached findAll() while the specialty list arrives from a separate SpecialtyRepository load - two distinct instance graphs over the same rows. Reference matching silently yields a directory in which no specialty has holders, which renders as a plausible-looking page rather than as a failure.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory indexes holders by Specialty.getId(). The rule is recorded in docs/system-design.md Contracts as a project-wide fact, not only as a note on this type, and a test pins the cross-load case.

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory or its nested pairing type declared package-private for minimal surface. Thymeleaf reads model attributes through SpEL reflection, which fails on accessors declared in a non-public class - which is why Vet, Specialty, and Vets are all public.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory and its nested pairing type are public. VetController and SpecialtyRepository keep their existing visibility.

risks.risk: I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build on the new template. It flags any literal >text< in an HTML file under src/main that carries no #{...} or th:text, and it flags any key present in messages.properties but missing from a locale bundle.
risks.mitigation: Every fixed string in specialtyList.html resolves through #{...}, and all three keys it needs already exist in every bundle, so the slice adds no key and touches no bundle. Specialty names and veterinarian names come from the model through th:text and stay untranslated, which is what REQ-LANG-002 requires.

risks.risk: Ordering left to the persistence layer or to HashSet iteration, making the page unstable across requests.
risks.mitigation: Specialties are ordered by the repository's ORDER BY name. Veterinarians under each specialty are ordered inside SpecialtyDirectory.of by last name then first name - VetRepository.findAll() returns an unordered Collection and Vet.specialties is a HashSet, so neither can be relied on.
